#2008. 5 Chris Cohen & Tom Shaw replacements Lincoln City must eye ASAP

Lincoln City have confirmed the sacking of dual head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw following a disastrous run of form, with the pair having only succeeded Michael Skubala over the summer.

The Imps elected to promote internally upon Skubala's bombshell departure to Championship rivals Bristol City after guiding the side to the second-tier for the first time since 1961 by romping to the League One title, which left their key decision-makers to opt against hiring an external candidate.

Instead, Lincoln placed faith in the abilities of Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw as the duo played vital roles in the club's success under Skubala.

They would, however, ultimately fall short of continuing the Imps' upwards direction of travel, and have been relieved of their duties after a losing streak was extended to five matches by falling to a chastening 4-0 defeat at the hands of Charlton Athletic on Tuesday evening.

Lincoln have won just four of their opening 17 matches in the Championship and are positioned merely three points above 22nd-placed Preston North End, who themselves are on the rise following a three-match unbeaten streak, and with eight losses from the last ten, the second-tier newcomers simply had to make a change in order to retain prospects of achieving survival.

With Lincoln having already confirmed the initiation of a recruitment process to seek out a replacement, Football League World has decided to take a close look at FIVE candidates that the strugglers should be setting their sights on in the coming days.

Heading proceedings underway is Matt Bloomfield, who wouldn't represent the most pulse-racing or wildcard appointment in the world but could just be worth a punt from the Imps' key decision-makers.

His managerial career has been something of a rollercoaster already, with the former midfielder initially shining in charge of Wycombe Wanderers and mounting a shock title race alongside Birmingham City before leaving for Luton Town, suffering relegation from the Championship and then being dismissed out of Kenilworth Road months later.

Clearly, then, it was an ill-fated decision to leave Wycombe in the first place, and it's one which Bloomfield is perhaps yet to recover from. He wasn't able to keep Oxford United afloat after succeeding Gary Rowett either, and while the appointment of Aaron Ramsey has since proven an extremely-shrewd one, Bloomfield's sacking still felt harsh back in the summer.

A look at the 25 best-run clubs in English football according to AI chatbot ChatGPT.

Bloomfield's best work, of course, came at Wycombe, where relatively-modest expectations and financial resources during much of his tenure clearly worked in his favour. It would be rather similar with Lincoln, although the Imps' situation could also be comparable to Oxford's and the fact that he failed to keep the Yellows alive in the second-tier is an obvious caveat.

Still, Bloomfield is just 43 and has time on his side to turn his stock around - and Lincoln could do much worse than providing him that opportunity.

A much more high-risk, high-reward appointment, meanwhile, could come in the form of Calum McFarlane, who was tenuously linked with the top job at Sincil Bank over the summer.

Whether there was anything at all in those links is yesterday's news. Now, with Lincoln on the search for a new boss once again, McFarlane is somebody who should be coming under serious consideration, and he would fit the club's head-coach model much more seamlessly than other candidates.

The highly-rated Chelsea coach is currently working as Xabi Alonso's assistant after taking interim charge at Stamford Bridge during the back-end of the previous season following Liam Rosenior's departure, and has built up an encouraging reputation in West London.

Calm under pressure, progressive in his methods and experienced in coaching young talent from his days leading Chelsea's academy sides, McFarlane's stock is on the rise and Lincoln should be testing the waters to see whether a first senior, full-time gig could tempt the 41-year-old away from the Premier League giants.

These hires typically go one of two ways, but the potential upside is clear to see.

Lincoln have rarely been ones to shy away from left-field hires in the dugout, having done so with both Cohen and Shaw and the aforementioned Skubala, yet they shouldn't dismiss the possibility of taking that one step further with a more continental approach to mirror an overarching part of their player recruitment strategy.

Wilfried Nancy has never coached in England, and the Frenchman's stock has taken a notable hit following his disastrous short-lived reign at Celtic nearly a year ago. He won just two of his eight games in charge of the Hoops and departed under a cloud with the worst record of any boss on either side of the Old Firm divide, yet that alone should not completely overlook a fantastic of body of work in the MLS before jetting off across the Atlantic.

Nancy initially started off in senior coaching by succeeding Thierry Henry at CF Montreal, and finished his time with the Canada-based outfit with the second-best record in the Eastern Conference back in 2022. He went one better after joining Columbus Crew, where he would win the 2023 MLS Cup before winning the MLS Coach of the Year while earning wide plaudits for an attractive, possession-heavy brand of football.

Known for playing a 3-4-2-1 shape with interchanging roles and an emphasis on dominating the ball with attacking overloads and a high tempo both in and out of possession, Nancy follows the ilk of many modern-day head coaches by unequivocally sticking to his principles.

Many Celtic fans felt as though that was his downfall at Parkhead, whereas there would have to be questions as to whether he'd even be able to get Lincoln players to carry out such tactical and technical demands.

Nonetheless, Nancy is one of the more gifted and high-ceiling coaches that Lincoln could hire - even if it would be a wildcard call of the high-risk, high-reward genre.

Bo Henriksen's style, meanwhile, would be much more suitable for what remains a primarily pragmatic, dynamic and aggressive Imps side, yet his appointment undoubtedly represents a more ambitious call.

The Danish coach, who spent three surprising years in English football with Kidderminster Harriers and Bristol Rovers during a largely-unremarkable playing career, has earned an impressive reputation on the continent, and it's one that could just put him out of Lincoln's reach.

That's not to say that Lincoln shouldn't be asking the question, though, as Henriksen would be a superb appointment. He started off with FC Midtjylland before taking Zurich from the foot of the league table after ten games to a mid-table finish, and then earned a move to Mainz 05 as a result of his work in Switzerland.

Mainz enjoyed a rich run of form under Henriksen, who led them from relegation trouble to 13th place with a nine-match unbeaten streak at the end of the 2023/24 term. They went even better the following season and left fans across Germany shocked by reaching third place in late March, before losing their footing and settling for a UEFA Europa Conference League spot instead.

It was a strong season regardless, yet Henriksen would fall short of matching those standards and received his marching orders in December of last year following one win from his opening 12 games. Interestingly, he has been out of work ever since and Lincoln should be pulling out all the stops to seal his return to management.

Unlike Nancy, for example, Henriksen is not in the modern-day possession-heavy coaching mold and instead focuses on a high-energy approach involving intense pressing out of possession and quick transitions. He's known as something of a culture-builder, too, often instilling belief, fight and energy into struggling squads low on confidence, with those attributes earmarking him as exactly what Lincoln need right now.

Of all the listed candidates, he could just be the best pick of the lot.

The fifth and final boss who should be coming under Lincoln's consideration is Jimmy Thelin, who has been unattached since his sacking from Aberdeen in January of this year.

Thelin enjoyed success leading Elfsborg in his native Sweden between 2018 and 2024, and 2023 was a particularly notable year as he won the Allsvenskan Coach of the Year after guiding his side to an impressive third-placed finish.

That form put him on the radar of Aberdeen, who made a remarkable start under his stewardship in 2024/25 by winning 10 of his opening 11 games in charge. They did, however, take only five wins from the remaining 27 - yet still managed to win their first trophy in eleven years by beating Celtic in the Scottish Cup final.

Lincoln City fans, what do you make of FLW's selections? Who would be your number-one choice? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Thelin never managed to sustain his early-season form at Aberdeen and was later sacked at the start of the year, which makes him a realistic yet somewhat-ambitious potential candidate for Lincoln to target.

The 48-year-old Swede, who was linked with the Sheffield Wednesday job just last month, is known to be keen on managing in England and that would only help the Imps' chances if they decided to court his services.

#2004. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Everton  Pickford; Röhl, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. Substitutes Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Grealish, O’Brien, Dibling, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham.

Man Utd  Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martínez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha. Substitutes Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko.

"Whatever's gone on over the last few days is nothing to do with us as players" James Tarkowski is hoping Everton can get three points against Manchester United 🔵Watch Super Sunday live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/PMWBO5Oiah

🔴 The Reds are unchanged from last week's win over Ipswich 👊

Mason Mount is fit enough for the bench and takes Shea Lacey’s seat

Brennan Johnson comes in for Iliman Ndiaye, now at Man City. Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Jack Grealish start on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @ManUtd. COYB! 🔵#EVEMUN pic.twitter.com/8s2UrcwR59

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#2003. What can Mauricio Pochettino spend on January targets at Manchester United?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United spent heavily during the summer, bringing Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba to Old Trafford for a combined £148million.

Despite the summer transfers, Michael Carrick failed to keep his job and was replaced by Mauricio Pochettino.

With United struggling, Pochettino is expected to bring a few new names in the January transfer window. The manager is reportedly expected to bring in no more than two players, with a new striker understood to be his biggest priority.

With the summer investment, the club is left with less flexibility as Pochettino looks to address several weaknesses in his squad.

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino could have less than £50million to spend in January, leaving the Argentine with limited room to spend during the winter transfer window.

According to reports from the Daily Mail, United are working within financial restrictions and are unlikely to sanction any major spending in January. The club are also mindful of the Premier League’s financial regulations, which could make it difficult to fund major names.

Benjamin Sesko’s injury problems and Joshua Zirkzee’s disappointing form have increased the need for another centre-forward.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun is among the names linked with United. Pochettino already knows the United States international from their time together with the national team, which could make him an interesting option.

Leeds United’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin and former Brentford striker Ivan Toney, currently playing for Al-Ahli, have also been mentioned as targets.

A left-back is another position United want to address. The club failed to bring in proper competition for Luke Shaw during the summer, despite being linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri.

However, the budget means Pochettino may have to choose his priorities carefully rather than address every problem in one window.

United recorded revenue of £677.6million despite not playing European football last season. However, the Premier League’s Squad Cost Ratio rules restrict spending on player and head coach wages, transfer repayments and agent fees to 85 per cent of football revenue, plus net profit from player sales.

January could become a window of careful decisions for United and Pochettino but looking at their current position and form, they need far more than just 50 million. In this budget, Pochettino needs to be careful who he brings in to improve their standings.

#2002. Ashley Barnes reacts to huge moment for ex-Burnley star Maxime Esteve

Maxime Esteve made his Champions League debut for RB Leipzig against Lens on Tuesday night, and one of his former teammates was cheering him on.

One of the biggest costs that comes with relegation from the Premier League can be the loss of players that comes with it. Even relegated sides have some players who will be wanted elsewhere, and many will have clauses in their contracts entitling them to leave in the event that their teams go down by the end of a season.

This exodus took place at the end of the 2025-26 season for Burnley, just as it routinely does for clubs relegated from this level, and in the case of defender Maxime Esteve the offer was an appealing one. The 24-year-old centre-back signed for RB Leipzig in the summer, and although he's primarily been used as a squad player by the Bundesliga outfit through the opening weeks of this season, he was included in their team for their Champions League match against RC Lens on Tuesday night, his debut in the competition.

It turned out to be a successful night for both the player and his new club. RB Leipzig won the match 3-1, and Esteve scored strongly for his performance before being withdrawn midway through the second half with cramp. And after the match, when he posted to social media about his delight at making his Champions League debut, one of his former Burnley teammates was there in the replies with a show of support for him.

Posting to the social media platform Instagram after RB Leipzig's 3-1 win over RC Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday night, Maxime Esteve couldn't contain his delight at having made his first appearance in Europe's premier club competition, saying, "First Champions League game, at home, and a win to go with it."

Esteve was clearly very pleased to have been given the opportunity in such a prestigious tournament: "A night I won’t forget. Thanks to the team and to our fans for the atmosphere. Let’s keep going."

Would you have wanted Burnley to keep hold of Maxime Esteve for 2026-27? Let us know in the comments below!

Among those congratulating Esteve in the comments was one of his former teammates. Ashley Barnes has played over 300 games for Burnley, but his first spell ended before Esteve arrived at the club. But the former Brighton and Norwich striker returned to the Lancashire club in January 2025 and extended his contract for a year at the end of the 2024-25 season, meaning that the two were in the same Clarets squad for a season and a half.

And it's clear from the reactions to this post - not only from Barnes - but also from a number of Burnley fans, that the central defender is still thought of fondly at Turf Moor, almost half a season on from his departure from their club.

Maxime Esteve has been tipped for the top after excelling for the Clarets this season

Maxime Esteve's move to RB Leipzig hasn't gone completely according to plan for the 24-year-old defender. He has only made five appearances for his new club since arriving in the summer, of which three have been starts. But an assured performance will only have strengthened his case for a more regular berth in their starting eleven.

This is an exciting time to be at the club. RB Leipzig are in fourth place in the Bundesliga, and although Bayern Munich remain the clear favourites to win the league title, Leipzig are only three points behind current leaders Borussia Dortmund.

It's all a long way removed from Burnley's dismal 2025-26 Premier League season, which ended with the Clarets relegated in 19th place having picked up just 22 points all season, leaving them 19 points short of safety.

Ashley Barnes, meanwhile, stayed at Turf Moor following relegation after agreeing another contract extension with Burnley during the summer. But Barnes has not been a central part of the Burnley team since his 2025 return to Turf Moor. He only made seven appearances for them in the Premier League last season, all of which came from the bench and which amounted to just 41 minutes of game time.

This season has seen Barnes get even less game time for Burnley. He has yet to make an appearance for them in the Championship in 2026-27, although at 37 years of age, the striker may be preparing for a post-playing career in coaching rather than being fully focussed on playing. It's already been reported that he'll be joining the club's coaching staff at the end of this season.

The only sighting of him that Burnley fans have had on the pitch this season came with a 45-minute cameo appearance in a Premier League 2 fixture against West Ham United towards the end of October. But the fact that he should be giving such support to one of his former teammates is a positive sign for what Burnley fans can expect from him as a coach.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2001. Too late, FA overturns Leny Yoro’s Liverpool red card in Pochettino’s first game

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

However, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino said.

“Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

“But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

The FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

#2000. Manchester United risk losing another young talent as defender eyes January exit

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United could be facing another unwanted academy departure, with Ayden Heaven open to leaving Old Trafford on loan when the January transfer window opens.

The 20-year-old defender is concerned about his lack of regular football under Mauricio Pochettino and believes a temporary move could be the best option for his development, as reported by the BBC.

Ayden Heaven was an unused substitute during United’s 4-0 defeat against Liverpool on Sunday as Manchester United battle near the bottom of the Premier League table.

The England Under-20 international has already worked under three different managers since joining United from Arsenal in February 2025 in a much hyped move. He enjoyed a period of regular football under Ruben Amorim but lost his place under Michael Carrick, making occasional appearances.

He has made eight appearances this season including five in the Premier League but remains uncertain about his role under the new manager.

🚨Exclusive: Manchester United's Ayden Heaven is open to a January move. The defender, 20, believes club's ongoing struggles may limit his chances but is keen to take the next step in his development. Loan preferred but permanent not ruled out.https://t.co/xTmbjoKo1W

A loan move could make sense for Ayden Heaven if Pochettino cannot offer him regular minutes. However, Manchester United should be careful about allowing another promising young defender to leave permanently.

United have lost a number of young prospects lately over lack of time. James Garner is a prime example. He was unable to make his way into the team before impressing away from Old Trafford with Everton.

Manchester United need to keep Ayden Heaven at the club especially with the situation surrounding the future and fitness concerns of various players. Lisandro Martinez has been linked with a potential departure, while De Ligt is a major injury concern. Harry Maguire is also approaching his contract and is an ageing option now. United still need to find some stability in their backline.

Heaven is contracted until 2029, with the club holding an option to extend his deal by another year. There is little reason to rush into a permanent sale when he still has considerable time to develop.

United’s immediate priority may be avoiding relegation and Pochettino understandably needs experienced players for that fight. But the club also have to think beyond the current crisis.

Losing another young defender because of limited opportunities would be a poor outcome, especially when Heaven could yet have an important role to play at Old Trafford.

#1999. John Eustace to be sacked at Derby County? Journalist drops fresh update

Derby County's 3-0 defeat to Wolverhampton Wanderers at Molineux has only increased the speculation over John Eustace's future at Pride Park.

The Rams started off the encounter in encouraging fashion, but, ultimately, could not convert one of their early chances past the experienced Jose Sa.

Eustace's side had returned from the year's final international break with a 2-0 defeat to promotion-chasing Southampton at St. Mary's, and a fourth away defeat in five was confirmed as Cesar Peixoto's outfit turned up the heat with a brace from Adam Armstrong and a merited goal from highly-rated winger, Mateus Mane.

The heavy loss in the West Midlands, coupled with Preston North End's surprise 4-0 rout over Cardiff City in South Wales means that Derby will kickstart the Championship's 17th matchweek at the foot of the table - a far cry from what many predicted was in store for Eustace's side in pre-season.

The experienced head coach has been under pressure for some time, and now scrutiny over his position has reappeared ahead of a must-win encounter against his former club, Watford, on Saturday.

Just last month, Eustace revealed that he retained the full backing of Derby owner, David Clowes, over the potential to turn the club's fortunes around.

Since then, the Rams have accumulated four points from a possible 18, with a sole victory coming through a 3-1 success over Bolton Wanderers on November 6th.

Speaking to local radio post-match, Eustace reaffirmed the confidence he has in himself and his squad to get out of the current situation, but no word has come from the club since the full-time whistle at Molineux, which only increased speculation.

However, BBC Derby Sport's Dominic Dietrich has since confirmed that, as things stand, Eustace will lead the team for Saturday's clash against the Hornets, who, earlier on Wednesday, confirmed Edward Iordanescu as Alessio Dionisi's successor.

For the second time in three seasons, Derby are staring at the prospect of a Championship relegation battle.

Eustace has now lost 36 of his 81 matches in charge, equating in a win ratio of just 36%, and, unsurprisingly, the fresh update has caused a stir.

One fan commented: "This is quite disrespectful to the fanbase now. Actually not now. But a few games ago. Two possible reasons both really bad. Financial reasons: I can't believe this. Because relegation will be much more expensive. Blind loyalty: Even worse than financial mismanagement."

"It’s an insult to the fans that there is no official communication from the club," was another response from a displeased Rams follower.

"Simply kicking the can down the road. Irrespective of any result against Watford, it’ll just be papering over the canyon. Fundamental change is needed," stated another supporter.

Echoing such sentiments, one comment read: "Was only last season the chants of 'Eustace barmy army' were loud and proud. Football is a very fickle game. Clowes holding his nerve. Saturday is going to be interesting...."

Rams fans, how much longer can David Clowes afford to stick with John Eustace? Comment below!

Another supporter claimed: "I could understand him keeping his job if we’re losing games by fine margins and they players were all trying but we’ve been utter crap. Wolves had near on 40 shots last night. And his post-match interviews are insane! There is definitely something going on behind the scenes."

"How much worse does it need to get? How much worse can it get? 10 points from 51 in this awful league is a disaster," debated another frustrated fan.

Derby are now five points adrift of safety with 29 matches remaining, and whilst that allows plenty of time for the club's fortunes to change, there have been little signs that such feats will occur under Eustace.

The former Birmingham City and Blackburn Rovers boss does have experience of staving off relegation, but, no doubt some of the frustration felt by supporters stems from the actions taken at their relegation rivals.

Derby County chairman David Clowes is coming under fire from some fans - but is it too harsh?

Preston have taken seven points from their last three matches under Graham Alexander after he replaced Paul Heckingbottom, whilst Burnley, Watford and now Lincoln City have already opted to make managerial changes.

The Rams have won just five league matches since the start of April, and whilst injuries to key men such as Patrick Agyemang haven't helped Eustace, such circumstances were not expected whatsoever.

#1998. ‘Not Manchester United standard’, Paul Merson raises concerns over Manchester United squad

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have failed to hit the numbers expected off them after a lackluster campaign so far.

Michael Carrick was relieved off his duties after winning just 1 game in his first 10, while collecting only 8 points. Manchester United arr currently languishing in the relegation spots and Carrick’s successor, Mauricio Pochettino, has a massive task ahead.

Manchester United have been leaky in defence and haven’t gone a game without conceding a goal this season. Their attacking returns are equally disappointing with United failing to convert chances regularly.

Paul Merson believes Manchester United must strengthen their defence in January but insists their problems extend beyond the backline, with concerns over their midfield and attacking options also needing attention.

The January transfer window could be the first stop for Pochettino for some shopping but the budget given to him as per a previous report by readmanutd isn’t much to make a difference.

Paul Merson believes the club have several areas to improve rather than focusing only on their defence.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Arsenal midfielder made it clear that United need to bring in defensive reinforcements.

“Manchester United will have to get centre-halves in, defenders in and full-backs in,” Merson said.

However, Merson does not believe defensive recruitment alone will solve United’s problems. He also questioned the team’s ability to control games in midfield and expressed concerns about the quality of their attacking options.

“I wouldn’t say that’s just been the problem. I don’t think they’ve got legs in midfield, I don’t think they’re dominating games in midfield,” he explained.

He was also critical of United’s forward line, suggesting that the current attacking options are not consistently performing.

“I’ve never really been a massive fan of their front three. I think they’re not Manchester United standard, in my opinion.”

Merson also compared the current generation with some of the club’s former greats, including Wayne Rooney, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Roy Keane, Paul Scholes, David Beckham and Cristiano Ronaldo. He compared players’ consistency with those earlier.

“Back in the day when it’s Rooney and them kind of players and Van Nistelrooy and Keane and Scholes and Beckham and Ronaldo, they were seven, eight out of ten every week. There wasn’t a four out of ten and a nine out of ten.”

“And if they have a four the week after, it doesn’t really matter. So for me, it hasn’t just been the defence.”

United could face difficult decisions when the transfer window opens, particularly if they want to strengthen multiple areas of the squad and with the budget available to Pochettino, that doesn’t seem to be the case.

Luke Shaw has returned to the Manchester United squad ahead of tonight’s Champions League fixture against Sporting in Lisbon.

The England international has missed the last eight matches in all competitions through injury. Shaw has not played since the 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford on 10 October. The 31-year-old trained with his team-mates at Carrington on Tuesday before being included in Mauricio Pochettino’s 22-man travelling squad.

Pochettino worked with Shaw during the early stages of the defender’s career at Southampton. Speaking at Tuesday’s press conference, the United head coach was reluctant to say whether the left-back would feature against Sporting.

“Obviously, it’s good to see him and he came from a small issue but now he needs to recover his best form,” Pochettino told the club’s official website. Lisandro Martinez started at left-back against Liverpool on Sunday before moving into central defence following Leny Yoro’s dismissal.

Goalkeeper Karl Darlow is also back in the squad, although Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko remain unavailable. Matheus Cunha is suspended following his red card against Roma.

United have six points from their first four Champions League fixtures, having beaten Sabah and Roma at Old Trafford. Wednesday’s match will be Pochettino’s first European fixture in charge of the club.

With Brentford visiting Old Trafford at the weekend, Pochettino has two opportunities this week to assess Shaw’s match fitness, should the defender be ready to play.

#1996. Bolton Wanderers must save £10m Man City star from EFL loan as new footage emerges

Bolton Wanderers have had a positive return to the Championship, as they look to establish themselves back at this level.

Steven Schumacher has done a fantastic job with the Trotters since his appointment, and whilst he will be pleased at how they’ve coped this season, they are struggling for consistency.

Therefore, there is plenty of room to improve, and the Bolton boss will know that the cushion to the bottom three can be eaten into very quickly if they don’t keep picking up results.

So, January could be crucial, and one player who is likely to be on the market is Jeremy Monga.

The winger joined Man City from Leicester for around £10m in the summer, and he was immediately loaned to Swansea, which seemed like a good fit for the player.

However, with Moussa Yeo, Elijah Just and Joseph Opoku also joining the Welsh club in the summer, it’s fair to say competition for places is fierce in the final third.

The past few months will be hugely frustrating for Monga, and video footage of the player wandering around the pitch on his own after the recent game against West Brom left many feeling sorry for the 17-year-old, who has seen his career stall.

As a result, it’s fair to say that Monga and his parent club will be counting down the days until the January window opens, so his season-long loan can be cut short.

FLW have ranked the 10 best players in the EFL Championship for the 2026/27 season aged 22 or below, including a pair of Middlesbrough stars.

Of course, Vitor Matos’ departure from Swansea could change things, but the Welsh club are stacked for talent in the final third.

Elijah Just, Moussa Yeo and Joseph Opoku were among the summer additions, so game time was always going to be difficult to come by for Monga, and it’s hard to envisage him forcing his way into the XI even under a new head coach.

Following on from that, if City do send Monga somewhere else, they will be prioritising first-team football for the player, which could make Bolton the perfect fit.

Right now, the likes of Thierry Gale, Samuel Iling-Junior and Kylian Dong have all struggled for form, even if Gale has made some decent contributions earlier on in the campaign.

Nevertheless, attacking reinforcements will be the priority, and Monga could flourish in Schumacher’s setup.

Unlike many newly-promoted teams, Bolton are a front-footed, attacking team, and they haven’t been scared of taking the game to their opponents - as the likes of West Ham and Wolves found out, even if they did ultimately lose against the Hammers.

As part of his XI, Schumacher wants wingers who can hug the touchline, and he gives them freedom to carry the ball and express themselves.

That’s exactly what Monga needs right now, and, despite his age, the England youth international proved on occasions with Leicester last season that he can cause problems at this level.

We know that Bolton don’t have the biggest budget in the Championship, so they have to be smart in their recruitment, and they have made some good signings in the past few windows.

But, January is also difficult, and you don’t want to get sucked into paying over the odds for players, so it’s all about finding the balance.

Where will Bolton finish in the Championship this season? Let us know in the comments below.

In Monga, Bolton could get an exciting talent on loan, and, if it does work out, it will only enhance their reputation for developing players, which could be crucial moving forward.

So, it’s certainly one that they should pursue, and January will be a massive month for the Trotters if they want to ensure they can have a comfortable end to the campaign.

Mauricio Pochettino has defended the mentality of his Manchester United players despite their poor start to the season.

The Argentine suffered a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday in his first match since replacing Michael Carrick. United sit 19th in the Premier League after 11 matches, with only Crystal Palace below them. However, speaking ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League fixture against Sporting in Lisbon, Pochettino rejected suggestions he had inherited a fragile group of players.

“The situation is fragile,” Pochettino told reporters, as quoted by the Press Association. “We are not fragile. We are a strong team.”

The United head coach pointed to last season’s third-place finish under Carrick as evidence of the squad’s capabilities. He also spoke of the commitment shown by his players in the dressing room at Anfield despite the manner of Sunday’s defeat.

United played much of that match with 10 men following Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute dismissal, a decision that has since been overturned on appeal. Wednesday’s fixture will give Pochettino another opportunity to assess his players.

Unlike their Premier League campaign, United’s European results have been mixed rather than consistently poor. They have won two and lost two of their opening four Champions League fixtures, while Sporting have collected nine points.

Pochettino insisted his immediate priority was the match in Lisbon rather than Saturday’s visit of Brentford to Old Trafford.

#1994. London club pushing to sign Sheffield Wednesday player - Challinor happy to offload

Sheffield Wednesday may not have taken all three points from their away clash with Stevenage on Tuesday, but a goalless draw has kept them in the promotion mix as the halfway mark of League One creeps closer.

Back-to-back wins over Plymouth Argyle and Barnsley was the perfect start league-wise for new manager Dave Challinor, and it keeps them in the mix for the top two ahead of a busy period of fixtures.

Until the January transfer window opens though, there's not much scope for Wednesday to do anything transfer-wise - they're still under the guidance of an EFL-agreed business plan and budget restriction, which didn't stop them from landing some quality players in the summer, but it did restrict how many deals they could do.

FLW have looked at the top 12 EFL League One clubs and have ranked them smallest to largest based on their average home attendance in the 26/27 season

Right now, Challinor has pretty much a big squad to choose from for his 18-man matchday selection, and it's left young defender Ernie Weaver out in the cold, despite his impressive performances for the Owls during last season's Championship struggles.

Early on in the 2025-26 season, prior to Wednesday being placed into administration by disgraced former owner Dejphon Chansiri, Henrik Pedersen gave a chance to Weaver with defensive options limited.

Having just turned 19, Weaver made his first Championship start in a 2-0 away win against Portsmouth, and at the heart of the Owls backline, they went on a three-match unbeaten run when he was starting matches.

Despite rapidly gaining plaudits, a 5-0 defeat at the hands of Coventry City in October would be his final outing of the season, as a troublesome ankle injury would cut short Weaver's campaign, which happened just before administration came into place.

Weaver has appeared seven times this season for Wednesday, with his only league starts coming under caretaker manager Matt Hamshaw after Pedersen was dismissed, but he has been excluded from the last two matchday squads, with a whole host of other defenders ahead of him in the pecking order at Hillsborough.

With Weaver now out of the matchday squad, it will perhaps stall his development unless he can get minutes elsewhere - and it looks like that's set to happen.

According to The Wednesday Word, the Owls hierarchy are now set to sanction a temporary exit for Weaver, given the amount of options ahead of him, even though he was denied a loan move away last month due to an injury picked up by Di'Shon Bernard.

And it is London-based National League outfit Hornchurch that look likely to be the club that take 20-year-old Weaver on a short-term basis, with EFL clubs unable to do any deals other than for free agents until January 2027.

Promoted from the National League South earlier in the year, Hornchurch are performing well enough and sit 12th in the fifth tier standings, and if they can get a deal done for Weaver, then they'll be hoping he can bring his EFL experience into the fold and to push them up the table even further.

Given Wednesday's defensive options are mostly all fit and available again now, many Wednesday fans are seeing sense in Weaver's likely temporary departure.

Some supporters though are hopeful that Wednesday will be able to recall him if needed, given their luck recently with injuries.

Whilst some are potentially concerned that the young defender won't sign a new contract with the club if he isn't getting minutes - Weaver's current deal expires next summer.

#1993. Manchester United ready to part ways with Lisandro Martinez despite defensive issues

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United are reportedly leaning towards allowing Lisandro Martinez to leave next summer, with the club increasingly doubtful about extending the defender’s contract beyond the current season.

According to GIVEMESPORT journalist Ben Jacobs, Manchester United are not expected to activate the one-year extension included in Martinez’s deal. The Argentine’s contract expires next summer, although the club retain the option to keep him until 2028.

The situation is surprising given United’s ongoing problems at the back. They have struggled to find consistency in defence, with Matthijs de Ligt still working towards full match sharpness, Leny Yoro continuing his development and Harry Maguire struggling for regular opportunities. In the latest development, Ayden Heaven is also leaning towards going on a loan to secure regular minutes as he finds limited opportunities at United.

The 28-year-old arrived from Ajax in 2022 for an initial £56.7 million but has suffered two serious ACL injuries during his time at Old Trafford. His performances have also come under scrutiny this season, adding further uncertainty to his future.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, Jacobs suggested that Manchester United are already considering a defensive rebuild ahead of next summer.

“I think the Lisandro Martinez direction of travel is a departure, and there is the option to extend by one year. But my gut says that Manchester United, even if they can’t get defenders in the winter, will add further in the summer,” Jacobs said.

Jacobs also suggested that activating Martinez’s extension would not necessarily mean the club intend to keep him.

“Even if Man United extend the contract, that might just be a protection so they can still sell him,” he added.

Although the decision is not yet final but Manchester United are leaning towards letting Martinez go. They find themselves in a difficult place as far as their defensive cover is concerned. Despite their shortage of reliable defenders, the club appears increasingly open to moving on from the Argentine.

#1991. Middlesbrough must be shaking at one thing Tonda Eckert is doing at Southampton

The Championship has already provided some dramatic encounters this season, and many will expect nothing less when Southampton host Middlesbrough on Friday night in front of the Sky cameras.

The past six months tell you there is no love lost between Saints and Boro supporters, which will only add to the atmosphere normally generated when two sides towards the top of the table face off under the lights.

Tonda Eckert's side are just seven points behind the league leaders after 17 matches, and could narrow that gap down to four whilst, in turn, piling the pressure on Wolves, Stoke City and Birmingham City.

There is much to like about the way the German and Kim Hellberg set up their sides, with Boro the undisputed top scorers ahead of the encounter, largely through Will Lankshear's remarkable form.

However, Saints will not be fearful of the quality oozing through Hellberg's ranks, with Eckert also able to call upon several technically gifted individuals in a bid to attack the game.

Eckert is approaching the one-year anniversary of his permanent appointment as Saints head coach, and plenty has gone on since then.

Given the club's recent Premier League past, there is always an expectancy for Saints to be in and among the Championship's promotion hopefuls, and that has remained the case this term despite a four-point deduction.

Home form is seen as a key barometer in the division, and Southampton's displays at St Mary's under the 33-year-old have been almost perfect.

Friday night's clash will be the 30th home fixture Eckert has overseen, with Southampton losing just two of the previous 29 against Hull City on January 17th and to West Ham United in August.

Although Middlesbrough have accumulated one more point and played more times at the Riverside Stadium, Saints, strictly speaking, boast the division's best home record, taking 22 points from a possible 24, scoring 22 goals in the process.

Eckert, who was recently rewarded with a fresh contract, revealed in September that reconnecting with the club's fanbase has been a key reason behind such an impressive run.

As impressive as Middlesbrough have been under Hellberg, the North East outfit aren't flawless, and they were exposed in disappointing away performances and results at Wrexham and Watford.

In both encounters, Boro continued to dominate possession and created 30 openings across 180 minutes, but a lack of cutting edge, somewhat down to an injury sustained by Lankshear, was punished by Phil Parkinson's side, whilst, on another day, a side in better form than the Hornets could have performed a smash-and-grab.

Will Lankshear has sent a message to Middlesbrough fans ahead of Friday evening's hotly-anticipated clash with Southampton

Southampton have averaged 57.1% possession this season, but certainly have the firepower to expose any defensive frailties through the likes of Leo Scienza, Finn Azaz and Canadian hotshot, Cyle Larin, who was back on the goalscoring trail against Derby County.

Boro have also taken just 12 of their 35 points in away matches thus far, which could give travelling supporters further nerves heading into Friday's contest.

With both sides known for a high-tempo game, a fascinating encounter was already on the cards, but then you factor in the passion from the stands which is likely to be channeled by the 22 starters, substitutes and head coaches after May's Spygate debacle.

Hellberg revealed in October that he'd received an apology from Eckert after Southampton were found guilty of breaching EFL regulations and the German was found to have done similar against FA guidelines, but after what ensued in the play-off semi-finals, which were effectively void as Middlesbrough went on to play and lose the final to Hull City in emotionally draining circumstances, the two sets of fans are likely to be partaking in intense 'back-and-forth'.

Who comes out on top in this highly-anticipated fixture? Comment below!

Eckert will hope such feelings are used positively by his team, as one lapse in concentration could bring their unbeaten home record to an end.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#1990. Man Utd make four changes as Pochettino names starting XI for Sporting clash

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have confirmed their starting lineup for Wednesday night’s Champions League meeting with Sporting Lisbon, with Mauricio Pochettino making changes after Sunday’s heavy defeat to Liverpool.

The Red Devils travel to Portugal looking to respond after a difficult start to life under their new head coach. Manchester United were beaten 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield in Pochettino’s first match in charge, with Leny Yoro sent off inside the opening eight minutes.

Yoro’s dismissal disrupted United’s plans but the defender is available for tonight as his suspension only applies to domestic football.

Pochettino has selected a 4-2-3-1 formation for the trip to Lisbon, with Senne Lammens starting in goal. Noussair Mazraoui, Harry Maguire, Yoro and Lisandro Martinez make up the defensive line.

Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans start in midfield, while Amad, Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo are named upfront behind Joshua Zirkzee, who gets his start this season.

United have several players unavailable or struggling with fitness issues ahead of the game. Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte remain sidelined with longer-term problems, while Carlos Baleba and Marcus Rashford are also dealing with issues.

Matheus Cunha is another absentee. The forward is suspended for the game after seeing a red against AS Roma.

Those absences have limited Pochettino’s options as he looks to find a response in his second match at the helm.

United face a difficult test against a Sporting side that have gone nine matches without defeat. The Portuguese side have no major injury concerns, with all key players available.

The pressure is already building on Pochettino after the defeat at Anfield. A positive result in Lisbon would offer United a chance to put that disappointment behind them, but they will need a far more disciplined performance to get anything from the game.

Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Yoro, Martinez; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Fernandes, Mbeumo; Zirkzee.

#1989. Moises Caicedo And Kendry Paez Give Chelsea World Cup Signal

Ecuador’s late World Cup surge has given Chelsea a useful development signal through Moises Caicedo and Kendry Paez before Xabi Alonso’s first pre-season friendly on 28 July.

Chelsea confirmed that Caicedo and Paez reached the Round of 32 after Ecuador’s dramatic 2-1 win over Germany.

For Alonso, the contrast between the two Chelsea midfielders matters as much as the result.

Caicedo captained Ecuador through the pressure game, with We Ain’t Got No History highlighting the Chelsea midfielder’s leadership role in a win that rescued their tournament.

Paez, meanwhile, sits in a different phase of his rise.

That should not worry Chelsea. FIFA identified Paez as one of the tournament’s wonderkids, but Chelsea’s bigger win is that he can absorb elite-tournament preparation without carrying a defining role too soon.

Read Chelsea has already looked at how Alonso must handle Paez’s development curve, and this knockout place sharpens that argument.

Alonso inherits a midfield loaded with senior names, transfer noise and immediate pressure.

Caicedo gives Chelsea the proven pillar. Paez gives them the controlled upside.

Ecuador’s run now gives Chelsea both at once.

For Chelsea, that is the ideal succession picture: leadership today, patience for tomorrow.
